Geographic focus:

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references March export restrictions, August shipment levels, pre-war margins
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — September export volumes, third quota batch expected within ~one month
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
China is maintaining stable refined fuel export volumes in September (~4+ million metric tons of gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel), broadly in line with August levels, as Beijing progressively eases export controls introduced in March following U.S.-Iran war disruptions to crude imports. Global refined fuel markets remain tight due to Russia's shift from exporter to importer (following Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries) and continued constraints on Middle Eastern fuel exports. Chinese refiners — predominantly PetroChina and Sinopec — are capturing elevated overseas margins (diesel export margins >1,500 yuan/ton; Asian diesel crack ~$70/bbl, 3x February levels). A third tranche of export quotas is expected within a month. Rising Chinese exports are expected to partially cap regional price gains in Asia.
